sources.title: GitHub repository metadata
sources.finding: Repository API reports 88155 stars at retrieval; this is popularity context, not a quality score.

sources.title: OpenHands README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: Canvas launches local Agent Server/automation services with Node 24 and uv, or optional Docker runtimes. Backends can live on laptop, remote VM or managed cloud. Same host workspace mounts still share files.

sources.title: OpenHands license
sources.finding: The cited root license governs this repository distribution, subject to component notices.

sources.title: OpenHands Agent Canvas
sources.locator: ACP; Where your agents run; Get started
sources.finding: Vendor describes desktop installs, ACP agents with existing subscriptions, extensions and local, self-hosted or managed backends.

sources.title: Agent Canvas architecture
sources.finding: Canvas renders conversations and controls backend APIs; execution, isolation and automation belong to separate runtime services.

sources.title: Agent Canvas self-hosting
sources.finding: User provisions and hardens a VM; public mode requires an API key, with TLS/firewall setup and shared-origin editor caveats.

sources.title: OpenHands Child conversations; Commits drawer; Goals; Export; Archive
sources.locator: Child conversations; Commits drawer; Goals; Export; Archive
sources.finding: Canvas child conversations stay linked and return results; local children may use isolated worktrees or shared workspace. Commit drawer shows diffs and agent Git/PR actions. Goals use a judge with round caps and user-message interruption. Transcripts export locally as Markdown/HTML with tool details; archive keeps backend history.

sources.title: OpenHands Persistent memory; MCP health; Per-backend settings
sources.locator: Persistent memory; MCP health; Per-backend settings
sources.finding: Canvas loads workspace/user persistent memory when enabled. Skills/MCP/secrets are backend-scoped. MCP health distinguishes reachable, rejected credentials and connection failure; public-server reachability does not verify credentials. Skills load on new conversation start.

sources.title: OpenHands Run statuses; Activity costs; Shared automation conversations; Export/import
sources.locator: Run statuses; Activity costs; Shared automation conversations; Export/import
sources.finding: Automations have pending/running/completed/failed/cancelled/skipped status; concurrency limits may skip runs. Activity exports CSV/JSON with numeric USD cost or null. Automations export/import versioned JSON; disabling preserves configuration. Other Cloud organization users can view run conversations read-only but cannot send messages.

sources.title: OpenHands Experimental critic; Iterative refinement
sources.finding: Experimental critic applies to OpenHands-agent conversations; ACP agents may not expose the path. Default threshold 0.6 and maximum three refinement attempts. Results expose score and detected issue categories; this is additional evaluation, not a successful acceptance-test result.

sources.title: OpenHands Tailscale; ngrok
sources.finding: Canvas documents phone/tablet browser access through Tailscale or authenticated public-mode ngrok; it does not establish native mobile apps.

sources.title: OpenHands Roles table; Private settings
sources.finding: Cloud/Enterprise organization roles are Member, Admin and Owner. Members create conversations and own private MCP/secrets/settings; Admins invite/promote users and manage LLM settings/credits; Owners delete organizations and claim Git organizations. Private settings remain private from other members including admins.

sources.title: OpenHands Plan cards; Comparison table
sources.finding: Canvas is free, MIT, single-user/shared-identity and self-hosted. Teams is $500 monthly for up to ten users with $50 monthly per additional seat, 5000 sessions per month, 30-day trial, RBAC and SSO/SAML. Enterprise has custom pricing. LLM keys are user-provided.

sources.title: OpenHands Enterprise managed gateway budgets; Usage; Why totals differ
sources.locator: Enterprise managed gateway budgets; Usage; Why totals differ
sources.finding: Enterprise managed-gateway budgets cap organization/user monthly spend. Gateway admits requests and can block at limits; direct provider calls are outside enforcement. Dashboard conversation estimates and gateway budget counters differ in scope/freshness. Spend may be live/stale/unavailable, not zero when unavailable; threshold alerts go to admins/owners.

sources.title: OpenHands docs/ACP_AGENTS.md
sources.finding: Local ACP agents reuse provider-native logins; clean containers/cloud need credentials. Pi/OpenCode are offered only on local/self-hosted backends. Same-provider conversations sharing container HOME can race on auth/config/lock files; Canvas cannot yet send SDK per-conversation data-dir isolation. Agent choice is per backend and running conversations retain their original agent.

sources.title: Agent Canvas app settings analytics switch
sources.locator: src/routes/app-settings.tsx lines 112-136 and 217-231 (enable-analytics-switch), release v1.38.0 commit e14b76c
sources.finding: App settings render a 'send anonymous usage data' switch that defaults on and saves user_consents_to_analytics and the telemetry consent as granted or denied. On a Cloud backend the switch is disabled and stays on.

sources.title: Agent Canvas telemetry consent modal
sources.finding: A telemetry consent modal asks the user whether to send anonymous usage data and saves the choice as granted or denied.

sources.title: OpenHands Enterprise SAML SSO guide
sources.finding: The guide explains how to let users of an OpenHands Enterprise installation sign in through a corporate SAML identity provider such as Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or ADFS.

sources.title: OpenHands pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards and comparison table (Agent Canvas, Teams, Enterprise)
sources.finding: Agent Canvas is free and MIT licensed. Teams costs 500 USD per month for up to ten users plus 50 USD per extra seat and lists SSO/SAML and RBAC; Enterprise has custom pricing. The page returns HTTP 403 to some automated fetchers but loads with a browser user agent.
